title: Planning run contract decomposition
description: Objective: split the oversized planning-run contract by contract responsibility without changing its public surface. Deliverable: packages/core/src/planning/planning-contract.ts becomes a compatibility type facade over new planning-command-contract.ts and planning-event-contract.ts; all three files stay <=250 lines and every existing import through planning-contract.js remains valid. Hard dependency: the already-landed planning lifecycle bytes in commit bcdc2f6. NOT in scope: reducer behavior, graph-revision behavior, root package exports, new commands/events, or policy changes. Owned paths: packages/core/src/planning/planning-contract.ts, packages/core/src/planning/planning-command-contract.ts, packages/core/src/planning/planning-event-contract.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: planning-contract.ts remains the compatibility facade and exposes the same complete set of public planning-run type names with unchanged shapes.
Commands/witnesses and state/events/results are separated into the two named modules without a dependency cycle or runtime authority change.
Each changed/new TypeScript file is <=250 physical lines, and existing planning tests pass unchanged.
The focused core typecheck and test command exits 0 with only the three owned paths committed.
taskRails: Refactor-only: preserve public types, stable error codes, check precedence, event/result ordering, deep freezing, and all observable reducer behavior.
Do not weaken, skip, rename, or delete behavioral assertions merely to make the split pass.
Every changed or new production/test TypeScript file in this task must be <=250 physical lines with LF/CRLF counted equivalently.
Use TDD/characterization and commit only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, merge, reset, or stash.

implementationPlan.description: Characterize the compatibility boundary before editing. From the committed `bcdc2f6` contract, inventory the exact 51 exported type/interface names and confirm the unchanged `packages/core/src/index.ts` planning export block names the same set; inspect every `./planning-contract.js` consumer and record that it is type-only. Treat the existing focused typecheck, planning-run reducer tests, and planning invariants as held-out characterization: do not edit root index, importers, reducers, or tests, and do not run the package gate yet.

Create `planning-command-contract.ts` by moving declarations without semantic edits: `PlanningRunKind`, `PlanningRunCommandKind`, all readiness/claim/release/recovery/submission/refusal/approval/activation/cancellation witnesses and proofs, `NodeSummary`, `PlanRevisionHashes`/`PlanRevisionSeal`, the private `PlanningRunCommandBase`, all twelve concrete commands, and `PlanningRunCommand`. Preserve exact readonly/optional fields, literal discriminants, union-member order, comments, and private visibility; import only the required `@moe/contracts` type(s). Keep the module <=250 physical lines and do not import the facade or event leaf.

Create `planning-event-contract.ts` for the observable lifecycle contract: move `PlanningRunLifecycle`, facets/state/successor data, the private event base, all eleven events and their union, and accepted/rejected/typed-UNSUPPORTED result types. Import required command-leaf types with a `.js` specifier and `RuntimeError`/`RUNTIME_LIFECYCLES` from contracts, yielding the one-way event->command dependency. Replace `planning-contract.ts` with an explicit type-only compatibility facade that names all 51 baseline exports from the two leaves—no wildcard or runtime re-export—and leave every existing consumer/root export unchanged. Keep both files <=250 lines.

Run the single shared-contract regression gate once after all moves: `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test`. Require exit 0; retain the fresh command, exit code, and output tail as `moe.complete_task` evidence. A failure is contract drift to diagnose in the three owned paths, not permission to edit or weaken existing tests.

Perform the one final adversarial review scoped to this refactor. Mechanically compare the facade's explicit name set with the 51-name `bcdc2f6` baseline and unchanged root index; inspect moved declarations for changed readonly/optional fields, discriminants, union order, private-base visibility, comments, runtime exports, or a facade cycle; use a cross-platform in-memory Node line counter to prove each owned TS file is <=250 for LF/CRLF/CR; confirm all non-owned importers/tests and root index are untouched and `git diff --check` is clean. If any byte is corrected, rerun the exact gate before completion. Then inspect `git status --porcelain`, stage/commit only the three explicit owned paths using an explicit pathspec (never broad add or bare commit), and verify `git show --stat` contains nothing else.

reopenReason: Human explicitly requested PLAN after being told this BACKLOG task required promotion; promoting the first ordered planning-file decomposition child.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use two explicit type leaves behind the existing facade. Rejected `export type *` because it would let future leaf exports silently expand the public surface; the facade must explicitly pin all 51 current names. Rejected rewriting the seven existing importers or root index because the task requires compatibility through planning-contract.js and owns only three paths. Rejected adding a new test file because existing reducer/invariant suites plus the unchanged root index already characterize the shared type surface, and test decomposition is a separate child task. Rejected any declaration cleanup/renaming while moving because this is a byte/shape-preserving refactor, not a contract redesign.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: planning-contract.ts currently exports exactly 51 types/interfaces, and packages/core/src/index.ts explicitly re-exports the identical 51-name set from planning-contract.js; leaving index.ts untouched makes the focused typecheck a compile-time public-export sentinel. Every direct consumer uses `import type`, and the root uses `export type`, so the facade must remain type-only and add no runtime surface. The acyclic leaf direction is planning-event-contract.ts -> planning-command-contract.ts -> @moe/contracts; neither leaf may import the facade. planning-command-contract owns kinds, witnesses/proofs/hashes/node summaries, private command base, concrete commands and command union. planning-event-contract owns lifecycle, facets/state/successor, private event base, events/event union and accepted/rejected/unsupported result union.
planningNotes.risks: Accidental public-name loss/addition, a leaf<->facade cycle, runtime re-exports, changed optional/readonly/discriminant/union-member structure, or moving private command/event bases into the public surface would violate the refactor contract. Preserve declaration bodies, property and union ordering, comments that explain typed UNSUPPORTED, and `.js` NodeNext specifiers. Count physical lines portably for LF/CRLF/CR and keep all three files <=250. Existing oversized tests are intentionally untouched here; their separate decomposition tasks own them.
